findings.mechanism: Node.js runs JavaScript on a single‑threaded event loop; using fs.writeFileSync and crypto.pbkdf2Sync performs blocking I/O and CPU‑bound work on that thread, stalling all other requests (03-concurrency-models).
findings.remediation: Replace fs.writeFileSync with await fs.promises.writeFile and replace crypto.pbkdf2Sync with crypto.pbkdf2 (promise version) or offload the PBKDF2 computation to a worker thread so the event loop remains non‑blocking.
findings.arithmetic: pbkdf2Sync with 600 000 SHA‑512 iterations ≈200 ms on a typical CPU; synchronous file write ≈5 ms; total per request ≈205 ms. With 5 concurrent requests the event loop processes them sequentially, giving latency ≈5 × 205 ms ≈ 1025 ms, so the 99th‑percentile latency exceeds 1 s.
